title: How ai-paint works
subtitle: A command-line paint tool for AI agents

scenes.heading: How ai-paint works
scenes.body: A command-line paint tool that an AI agent can use
scenes.narration: This video explains ai-paint, a command-line paint tool. An AI agent draws with it the way a person uses a canvas, one step at a time.

scenes.heading: A picture is a JSON document
scenes.body: A canvas size, a list of layers, and a list of operations.
scenes.narration: An ai-paint picture is a JSON file. It holds a canvas size, a list of layers, and a list of operations. Because the file is plain text, an agent can read it, change it, and save it again.

scenes.heading: Operations do the drawing
items: Drawn in order: a later operation lands on top
Layers stack in list order, bottom first
Hidden layers are skipped when rendering
Coordinates are pixels from the top-left corner
scenes.narration: Operations are drawn in the order they are listed, so a later one lands on top of an earlier one. Layers stack in list order, with the first at the bottom. A hidden layer is skipped. Coordinates count pixels from the top-left corner.

scenes.heading: What an operation can draw
items: Strokes, lines, rectangles, ellipses and polygons
Text, pasted pictures and erased areas
Speech balloons, limbs and smooth curves
scenes.narration: The operation types cover simple shapes, text, and pasted pictures. There are also speech balloons, limbs and smooth curves for characters, and an svg operation for detailed drawings written as SVG code.

scenes.body: For detailed drawings, especially characters, the svg op is the most flexible tool.
scenes.narration: The README gives this advice. For detailed drawings, especially characters, the svg operation is the most flexible tool. An agent can write SVG it already knows, and still use the layers, grid views and balloons around it.

scenes.heading: Drawing with SVG code
scenes.body: Markup inside a box on a layer. Scripts and outside links are refused.
scenes.narration: The svg operation takes SVG markup inside a box on a layer. The example anime girl defines her eye once and mirrors it with a use element, clips the iris to the eye white, and blurs the blush. Scripts and links to outside files are refused, and the drawing is rendered by the system's librsvg library.

scenes.heading: Change one thing, keep the rest
scenes.body: Each operation has an id. Update one by its id.
scenes.narration: Every operation has an id, so the agent can change one of them later and leave the rest of the picture as it was. This is what makes repeated edits practical.

scenes.heading: Limits to know
items: Canvas up to 10,000 pixels on each side
The built-in font covers Latin letters only
Existing operations cannot be rotated or scaled yet
scenes.narration: There are limits to know about. A canvas can be up to ten thousand pixels on each side. The built-in font covers Latin letters, so other scripts need a font file. Existing operations cannot be rotated or scaled yet.

scenes.heading: Try it
scenes.body: ai-paint new, ai-paint apply, ai-paint render
scenes.narration: To try it, create a new picture with the new command, apply a changes file with the apply command, and turn the result into a PNG with the render command.
